2. Reads local PKGBUILD and pyproject.toml files from the source tree to extract package metadata (names, descriptions, dependencies, optional dependencies)
3. Uses inline python3 -c commands with tomllib to parse TOML files - this is the upstream application's own code, reading its own configuration
4. Generates shell arrays (pkgname, _pkgdescs, _urls, _depends, _optdepends) from the extracted metadata
5. Uses sed to replace corresponding sections in the PKGBUILD with the generated content
6. Runs `makepkg -do` at the end, which is a standard build command

There are no network requests, no eval/base64/curl/wget patterns, no code exfiltration, no backdoors, and no system modifications beyond normal PKGBUILD updates. All file operations are local to the source tree. The Python code simply reads the package's own pyproject.toml to extract metadata - this is expected upstream packaging behavior, not injected malicious code. The `makepkg -do` invocation handles dependency downloading through standard makepkg mechanisms, which is normal AUR workflow.

This script automates routine maintainer tasks for generating PKGBUILD metadata from the package's source configuration, consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices.
</details>
